title: fix the compact discovery panel filters are getting cutoff on desktop
summary: Since the last plan (commit `da7ba50`), the only change is newer Seed Bible work merged in from the main line of development; the filter arrows themselves did not change. Nobody has tested the plan for `da7ba50` yet, so the tests marked new or changed since commit `c75c692` (the last plan that was tested) are still worth a careful look. On a desktop computer, the small "Discover" panel next to the Bible text has a row of filter buttons (like **All**, **Notes**, **Cross references**, **Study notes**). When there were more buttons than fit, the extra ones were cut off and there was no easy way to reach them with a mouse. Now, when the buttons don't fit, round arrow buttons appear on each side of the row: click them to move the row. When everything fits, no arrows appear. On phones and tablets the arrows stay hidden and you swipe the row instead.

links.label: Issue 1908: The compact discovery panel filters are getting cutoff on desktop

setup.title: Use a desktop or laptop computer with a mouse or trackpad
setup.body: Most tests need a computer browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari), with the window maximized. One section at the end needs a phone or tablet.

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Open the preview link above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, wait a few minutes and reload: the preview may still be deploying. If the page looks like an older version of Seed Bible, do a hard refresh: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, or **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac. A private/incognito window gives you a clean start.

setup.title: Open John 3 and find the Discover panel
setup.body: Open **John 3**. To the right of the Bible text there should be a box titled **Discover John** with a **+ Create** button and a row of rounded filter buttons below it. These rounded filter buttons are called "chips" in the tests below. If the box is below the Bible text instead of beside it, click the compass icon (**Discover content**) in the small toolbar above the text to move it beside the text. If there's no Discover panel at all, open **Settings** and make sure **Show discovered content** is turned on.

setup.title: Add a note so there are more chips
setup.body: In the Discover panel, click **+ Create** and save a short note (type `Testing filters`). If it asks you to sign in, sign in with your email and the code it sends you. After saving, the chip row should include a **Notes** chip. More chips make it more likely the row won't fit, which is what these tests need.

sections.title: Scroll arrows on desktop
sections.intro: The main change: arrow buttons for reaching filter chips that don't fit.

tests.title: Arrows appear when the chips don't all fit
tests.why: This is the problem from the issue: chips were cut off with no way to reach them using a mouse.
tests.before: You're on John 3 with a note added (see setup).
steps: Look at the chip row in the Discover panel.
Note whether the last chip is cut off at the right edge, or whether all chips are fully visible.
expected: If not all chips fit: a small round button with a left arrow sits at the left end of the row, and one with a right arrow at the right end. The left arrow is faded (there's nothing further left yet). The right arrow is solid.
If all chips fit: there are no arrow buttons at all. In that case mark this test **Blocked** with a note listing the chips you see, since the next tests need the arrows.

tests.title: The right arrow reveals the hidden chips one at a time
tests.before: The arrows from the previous test are showing.
steps: Click the right arrow once.
Keep clicking it until it fades out.
expected: Each click moves the row so the next chip that was cut off on the right becomes fully visible. The row jumps there at once rather than sliding smoothly.
Once the last chip is fully visible, the right arrow fades and clicking it does nothing.
As soon as the row has moved, the left arrow becomes solid.
tests.why: Changed since commit `c75c692`: the row now jumps straight to the next chip instead of gliding there.

tests.title: The left arrow slides back to the start
tests.before: You've scrolled to the end in the previous test.
steps: Click the left arrow until it fades out.
expected: Each click brings the previous cut-off chip on the left fully into view.
When **All** (the first chip) is fully visible again, the left arrow fades and the right arrow is solid again.

tests.title: Chips you scrolled to still filter the list
steps: Use the right arrow to reach the last chip.
Click that chip.
Use the left arrow to go back and click **All**.
expected: After clicking the last chip, it's highlighted and the panel shows only that kind of content.
After clicking **All**, it's highlighted and every kind of content shows again.

tests.title: Trackpad or Shift + mouse wheel scrolling keeps the arrows in step
steps: Move the pointer over the chip row.
Scroll sideways with a two-finger swipe on a trackpad, or hold **Shift** and turn the mouse wheel.
Scroll all the way to the end, then all the way back.
expected: The row scrolls, and no scrollbar appears under it.
At the end, the right arrow is faded and the left arrow solid. Back at the start, it's the other way round.

tests.title: The arrows can be used with the keyboard
steps: Click on the Bible text, then press **Tab** repeatedly until the right arrow button shows a focus outline.
Press **Enter**.
Keep pressing **Tab** to move through the chips.
expected: Pressing **Enter** on the right arrow slides the row, the same as clicking it.
When a chip that's cut off gets the focus outline, the row slides so you can see it.

tests.title: Arrows go away when the panel gets wide enough
tests.why: The arrows should only show when they're needed.
steps: Click the compass icon (**Discover content**) in the toolbar above the Bible text. The Discover panel moves below the Bible text and becomes wider.
Scroll down to the panel and look at the chip row.
Click the compass icon again to move the panel back beside the text.
expected: Below the text, all chips fit in one row and there are no arrow buttons.
Back beside the text, the arrows return if the chips don't fit, with the left arrow faded.

tests.title: Arrows update when you change chapters
tests.why: Changed since commit `c75c692`: the code review found the arrows could keep the previous chapter's state when the new chapter had the same number of chips but different ones. The new commit makes the arrows recheck whenever the chips themselves change. The intended scroll position when moving between chapters isn't spelled out in the PR, so flag anything that looks wrong.
steps: On John 3, scroll the chip row to the end with the right arrow.
Go to the next chapter, **John 4**.
Look at the chip row. Then go back to **John 3** and look again.
expected: On John 4 (which has no note from you, so likely no **Notes** chip), the arrows match what you see: no arrows if every chip is fully visible, arrows if any chip is cut off.
A faded arrow never sits next to a chip that's cut off on that side, and a solid arrow always moves the row when clicked.
Back on John 3, the same is true.

tests.title: Arrows update when you resize the browser window
tests.why: New since commit `c75c692`: the arrows now recheck whenever the browser window changes size.
tests.before: You're back on John 3, with the Discover panel beside the Bible text.
steps: Un-maximize the browser window and drag its right edge to make it narrower, a little at a time.
Then make the window wide again (or maximize it).
expected: Whenever chips are cut off, the arrows are showing, and clicking a solid arrow moves the row.
Whenever every chip is fully visible, there are no arrows.
If the panel moves below the Bible text as the window gets narrow, that's expected; the same rules apply there.

tests.title: Arrows update when you change the app's language
tests.why: New since commit `c75c692`: the code review found that switching the app's language (which makes chip labels longer or shorter) didn't make the arrows recheck. The new commit fixes this.
steps: On John 3, open **Settings** and find **Language**.
Choose a language with longer words, such as German (**Deutsch**).
Go back to John 3 and look at the chip row, then click the arrows if they show.
Switch the language back to English when done.
expected: The chips show their labels in the new language.
The arrows match what you see: showing (with a solid arrow that moves the row) if any chip is cut off, gone if every chip is fully visible.
After switching back to English, the same is true.

tests.title: The arrows look right in dark mode
steps: Switch Seed Bible to dark mode in its settings.
Go back to John 3 and look at the chip row.
expected: Both arrow buttons have a visible round background and a clearly visible arrow, matching the style of the chips next to them.
The faded arrow is visibly dimmer than the solid one.

tests.title: The arrows work when reading a right-to-left Bible
tests.why: Changed since commit `c75c692`: the code review found that with a right-to-left Bible (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu), both arrows showed faded and did nothing. The new commit is meant to fix this: the arrows now work in terms of "toward the start" and "toward the end" of the row, and their arrow icons flip to point the right way.
steps: Click the translation name at the top of the Bible text (for example **BSB**) and choose an Arabic or Hebrew Bible. Typing `Arabic` or `Hebrew` in the search box helps find one. If it asks **Switch language?**, choose **Don't Switch**.
Open **John 3** in that Bible. The chip row now starts from the right side, with **All** at the right end.
If arrow buttons show, click the solid one until it fades, then click the other one until it fades.
When done, switch back to the Bible you were using before.
expected: If not all chips fit: the arrow on the right is faded at first and the arrow on the left is solid. Clicking the left arrow moves the row to reveal the chips hidden off the left side, one at a time, and the right arrow becomes solid.
Once the last chip on the left is fully visible, the left arrow fades. Clicking the right arrow brings the row back until **All** is fully visible again.
Each arrow points the way the row moves when you click it.
If all chips fit, there are no arrows. Mark the test **Blocked** with a note if so.

sections.title: Phones and tablets
sections.intro: On touch screens the arrows are hidden, since you can swipe the row.

setup.title: Open the preview on a phone or tablet
setup.body: Open the same preview link on a phone or tablet. Open **John 3** and scroll down below the Bible text to the **Discover John** panel. If you added a note on the computer while signed in, sign in with the same account here so the **Notes** chip shows too.

tests.title: Chips can be swiped and no arrows show
steps: Look at the chip row.
Swipe the chip row left and right with your finger.
Tap a chip.
expected: No round arrow buttons appear on either side of the row.
The row slides with your finger if the chips don't all fit.
Tapping a chip highlights it and filters the panel.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: The rest of the Discover panel works as before
steps: On John 3 on the computer, look at the chips' size and spacing.
Click **+ Create**, then cancel without saving.
expected: Each chip is just wide enough for its label, with no text spilling outside its rounded edge.
**+ Create** opens the note editor, and cancelling returns you without adding a note.

notCovered: Screen reader labels for the arrow buttons ("Scroll filters left" and "Scroll filters right") aren't tested here. Testers who use a screen reader are welcome to check them.
The new automated tests for the arrows run in the code checks, not by hand.
Code cleanup in the same file (reformatting and removed comments) has no visible effect.

The other Seed Bible changes this branch brought in from the main line of development (for example the removed **Show All** button and friends' notes in the panel) are tested in their own pull requests.
